title: Sounds back, steadier screens
bullets: The ✅ and ❌ sounds, and the cheer at the end, play again.
In 🗣️ Say, the phrase stays still when you press Check; the pinyin just appears underneath.
❌ Not yet is a round button like ✅ I got it, and Keep going is tidier.
Coming back to Home is quicker.

title: A new look: the summit climb
bullets: Brighter colours: a green hill for Chinese, lilac for Math, and round buttons with a thick outline.
Progress is a trail of numbered stops up to a flag. Finished stops turn gold with a tick.
A stop you marked Not yet turns coral with a cross, so you can see which ones to try again.
A grown-up's attempt page has a results table: each item's tries as marks and a Control hit, Fixed or Go again pill.

title: Keep going lives on the lesson
bullets: Home shows each lesson once. A practice your child is in the middle of says Keep going, with their round and stars.
Lessons your child is in the middle of come first, newest at the top.
A 🔄 beside Keep going lets your child start that practice over, after asking first.
Grown-ups can stop all of a lesson's unfinished practice from Progress. It stays in history as stopped.

title: A new look: the exercise book
bullets: The whole app now looks like a school exercise book: green cover, ruled paper and blue ink for things you can press.
✍️ Write and 🖌️ Draw show each character on a 田字格 practice square.
Progress is a ruler that fills as you go, and a finished practice gets a red 优 seal.
The grown-ups area has the same look, with ruled menu rows.

title: Updates moved to What's new
bullets: The update prompt no longer appears on your child's Home screen. Updates are now applied from What's new in the parent area.
What's new lists every release, newest first, so you can see what an update brings before you install it.
A small dot on the gear and on the What's new menu entry shows that an update is waiting.

title: Clearer Tricks and smoother practice
bullets: 🧠 Tricks now shows the trick's name, the question on its own line, and a ? button that explains how the trick works.
A right answer on the second try now plays the happy chime, and the Check key shows a check mark.
⚖️ True? uses blue and orange buttons and gives only one try.
Pinching or double-tapping no longer zooms the screen in the middle of practice.

title: A steady blank, and problem counts
bullets: Math problems show the missing number as one box that stays the same size, instead of a question mark.
🧠 Tricks walks through each problem with a title and a hint for every step.
Settings has a new Problems per practice choice for math: 10, 15 or 20 (20 until you change it).

title: Math is here
bullets: Math is now a second subject, with the Fall 2026 math lesson for Grade 1 addition and subtraction.
Five ways to practice: ⚡ Facts, 🔍 Missing, ⚖️ True?, 📖 Stories and 🧠 Tricks.
The app checks the answers itself and gives a second try before showing the answer.
The parent area shows which kinds of problems are trickiest, and which answer was entered for a missed problem.

title: Draw plays by itself
bullets: 🖌️ Draw now starts drawing the character as soon as it opens; the only button is Replay.
New learners start with a half-second pause after each stroke. Learners you already set up keep their pause.

title: Learn the phrases first in Say
bullets: A new Learning setting turns 🗣️ Say into a gentle first look: each phrase is shown and heard, and your child taps Next.
Nothing is marked and no score is kept, so it does not count toward attempts.

title: Practice stays quick
bullets: Fixed a slowdown that built up after several 🖌️ Draw sessions in one visit, where the next character started drawing before its sound or played over the chime.

title: Draw: set the stroke speed and pause
bullets: Settings has new choices for how fast each stroke is drawn (Slow, Normal or Fast) and how long to pause after it.
Each learner has their own pace, and it applies the next time practice opens.

title: Draw and Say, with the Pre-K lesson
bullets: 🖌️ Draw shows a character being drawn one stroke at a time, so your child can copy each stroke on paper.
🗣️ Say shows a phrase to say aloud, then plays it so your child can check themselves.
A lesson can now offer several kinds of practice, and a new Pre-K lesson (2026-10-19) uses 🖌️ Draw and 🗣️ Say.
